result.killer: No outright killer. Weakening facts: (1) per Forvis Mazars, accounts are shown to DGAT on request and the activity report goes to the general assembly, and penalty texts were still pending; (2) the donor register must be a paper register stamped by a court; (3) the 31 March deadline was not found; (4) Compta Expert (SYCEBNL accounting software) covers the accounting part.
result.reason: No killer found: no DGAT e-filing portal (the 2026 OSC platform is for networking and information) and no OSC compliance pack. The duty looks softer than claimed, though. Two firm-written summaries, read via search results, say accounts go to DGAT only on request and the activity report goes to the OSC's own general assembly. Penalties were still to be set by later texts, and the donor register must be paper, stamped by a court. Not found: the 31 March date. AllAfrica does report an annual filing of activity and financial reports to the Interior Ministry. Compta Expert already covers SYCEBNL accounts. The ordinance, Mazars and Hivos PDFs would not open as text, so I could not settle the auditor threshold or penalties. Paying demand among about 14,000 mostly small OSCs is doubtful.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Searched friperie, used phones/electronics resellers, pawnbrokers (prêt sur gage), brocanteurs and police registers, and general used-goods trade rules. Found no Ivorian rule requiring second-hand dealers or pawnbrokers to keep a police-style register or file periodic reports. Pawn lending presumably falls under UEMOA/BCEAO microfinance rules, but no source on this (unverified). Friperie: the 1975 import ban (ordonnance 75-647) was cited, but no current friperie-specific licence or registry found. Used-phone resellers: the only sector duty is ARTCI pre-sale homologation of terminal equipment (decree 2013-301; ordinance 2012-293 art. 83), with a July 2024 warning about forged certificates; the 2019 GSMA 'We Care' stolen-IMEI blocking scheme puts no found duty on resellers. General duty on every trader: carte de commerçant (decree 2024-381 of 12 June 2024). A national trader census ran May-July 2026 (Unitec concession, field-based, 1.5 million target; 127,457 paid and 338,422 unpaid at 31 Jan 2026), so this is a generic state-run workflow, not a niche. Vehicle-age limit for used cars is category 5, not covered here. Nothing new beyond K04 for transport and no match to any known idea.

Export is only an aspiration. No mandatory recurring filing found. Not a viable software buyer group.

result.competitor: Compta Expert (Compta Expert Informatique / Cercle Gestion et Développement) is accounting software sold as SYCEBNL-compliant: built-in chart of accounts, automatic financial statements, sold to associations and NGOs on a lifetime licence (per ohada.com). Excel SYCEBNL templates are widely requested and used. Advisory firms such as Forvis Mazars sell compliance help, and DGAT, the EU-funded PASCI project and Save the Children run free workshops. No OSC-specific pack combining the ministry report, a digital donor register and AML checks was found, and no DGAT online filing portal was found.
result.duty: Ordinance 2024-368 of 12 June 2024 is in force, ratified by law 2025-386 of 11 June 2025. Per the Forvis Mazars summary, OSCs owe a yearly activity and financial report to the Interior Ministry/DGAT and must produce their accounts when DGAT asks. They must keep a donor register that identifies every donor, cash gifts included, and appoint an auditor above thresholds (balance sheet, resources, staff). Legacy OSCs had until 21 June 2025 to comply. Table of contents (loidici): Chapter 5 monitoring and evaluation (Art. 47–52), Chapter 6 penal provisions (Art. 53), and dissolution in Art. 6–24. The OHADA SYCEBNL act has also applied since 1 Jan 2024. Art. 17 requires every non-profit to keep a numbered, initialled donor register, and Art. 24 sets criminal penalties for leaders who fail to prepare financial statements or the activity report. Not verified: the 31 March deadline, penalty amounts and the auditor threshold. The ordinance PDF on the DGAT site is a scanned image and could not be read.
result.market: The figure of about 14,000 OSCs is attributed to the Interior Minister in the claim; I did not verify it. Many of these are small religious and community associations with little money.
result.reason: The duty is real. Ordinance 2024-368 was ratified in 2025, and DGAT ran workshops in San Pedro, Korhogo and Bondoukou in April–June 2026. Forvis Mazars says OSCs must send yearly activity and financial reports to the Interior Ministry and keep a donor register, and need an auditor above a threshold. The legacy-OSC deadline was 21 June 2025. Separately, OHADA's SYCEBNL accounting act has applied since 1 Jan 2024. It requires a numbered, initialled donor register and annual financial statements, with criminal penalties under Art. 24. SYCEBNL software already exists (Compta Expert, lifetime licence) and Excel templates are common, so the accounting core is partly covered. I found no OSC filing-pack or state portal. Not verified: the 31 March date, penalty amounts, the auditor threshold and the 14,000 count. Buyers are mostly poor, informal bodies with weak willingness to pay.

result.competitor: No Ivorian software, state portal or app was found that handles the taxe de nuitée or its monthly return. French-language PMS comparisons mention taxe de séjour and fiche de police only under French rules. Local Abidjan developers such as Kolonell sell custom-built or SaaS PMS (about 30,000 FCFA/month to 3.5-9M FCFA builds), with no mention of the nuitée tax. A Ministry of Tourism eTourism platform with payments has been announced, but nothing links it to this tax. Specific local PMS vendors were not checked one by one.
result.duty: The duty is real and in force. The taxe de nuitée was created by the tax annex to finance law no. 2025-987 of 19 Dec 2025, which has applied since 5 Jan 2026. Hotels and owners of furnished residences must collect it from guests when the bill is paid, then pay it to the municipal treasurer by the 15th of the following month. Rates per night: 500 FCFA (no star), 1,000 (1 star), 1,500 (2 stars), 2,000 (3 stars and above). For furnished residences the rate is set by each commune; in the Abidjan district it is 1,000 FCFA. Penalties, the filing format (paper or online), any official form, rates outside Abidjan and the fiche de police were not found. Separately, the tourism development tax (TDT) rises from 1.5% to 2.5%, but only for operators with turnover above 5M FCFA. Smaller operators, guesthouses included, pay instead a 100 FCFA communal contribution (contribution/taxe de l'entreprenant). The Ministry of Tourism's 18 Aug 2026 campaign concerns the TDT, not the nuitée tax.
result.market: The Ministry of Tourism counted 4,394 hotels (65,994 rooms) in 2021, and the minister cited about 4,500 in 2022. No breakdown by star rating and no count of furnished residences or Airbnb-type hosts was found. Most establishments are likely unclassified or low-star and partly informal.
result.reason: The duty is real, monthly and new, and no dedicated tool was found. The software job, though, is trivial: nights multiplied by a flat rate, plus a payment by the 15th to the municipal treasurer. Nothing suggests an e-filing channel a product could plug into, and no penalties were found. The buyers are about 4,500 mostly small, cash-based, partly informal hotels and guest houses. They are unlikely to pay for a tool just for this, and enforcement through the communes looks uneven. Generic or local PMS vendors can add a nuitée line easily. The idea is better as one feature inside a cheap mobile-money-friendly PMS or guest-register app than as a standalone product. The TDT increase mainly hits firms above 5M FCFA turnover.

A duty exists for diamonds: arrêté 502/MIM of 10 Nov 2014, under the 2014 Mining Code, covers approval of buying offices and buying/selling authorisation. I could not confirm that it is still in force. I found no current text on a gold purchase register, and no frequency or penalty. The SAVOD-CI union (June 2025) issues local buy/sell authorisations through sub-offices; that makes the state and the union the likely gatekeepers. No software for buying offices turned up in two searches, but the search was thin. The market looks small: the roughly 200 artisanal and 300 semi-industrial permits are miners, not buyers, and I found no register of buyers. The buyers are often informal. Low willingness to pay and a risk of state centralisation keep the score at 3.

result.competitor: None found for private software. The state Guichet Unique Automobile (GUA) and DGTTC handle registration and plates directly.
result.duty: Registration and secure plates for all 2- and 3-wheelers. Special operation for six months from 15 Oct 2026. Irregular engines can be confined and impounded. Flat-rate fees are to be published by the DGTTC.
result.market: Not quantified. No register figure found. August 2026 accident statistics show 2- and 3-wheelers are involved in about 55% of 1,657 accidents.
result.reason: Duty is real: a Ministry of Transport announcement of 18 Sept 2026 (Koaci, Benin Web TV) places irregular 2- and 3-wheelers under administrative confinement. A six-month special registration operation starts 15 Oct 2026. Secure QR-code plates were being fitted at the GUA in Bouake on 12 Sept. Fees are not yet published, and I found no official arrete text. The duty is one-off and temporary, not recurring. Owners deal directly with the state GUA. I found no private software competitor, but the buyer is informal, low-income and hard to reach, and the value is mostly a queue-and-paperwork service. The window is short, there is little recurring revenue, and a rule on intermediaries is unknown. A weak SaaS case. Related known id K04.

result.competitor: GDF Africa and Fleeti (GPS telematics); custom TMS builds (Kolonell); OIC digital DUT. No document-compliance tracker found.
result.duty: DUT per shipment (decree 2015-270); haulier access to profession (2015-269); visite technique periodic and required for insurance
result.market: Not found; no register or statistic located
result.reason: The duty is real. The DUT (decree 2015-270) is the only mandatory waybill for road freight, costs 2,500 FCFA, and is run by the OIC in paper and digital form. Visite technique is mandatory and checked: a 2026-10-01 koaci report describes a tow truck found overdue since Jan 2025, and an insurance link applies from Jan 2025. I found no tool for document-expiry tracking for small hauliers. Existing offers are GPS fleet telematics (GDF Africa, Fleeti) and custom builds. The score is low for three reasons. The per-shipment DUT is bought from the OIC and is not a recurring filing. Expiry alerts are weak value to pay for. Small owner-drivers are hard to reach and unlikely to pay. Penalties and the number of firms were not found. The decree fetch returned 404.

The duty is real: the 2014 Tourism Code requires prior authorisation from the ministry's Guichet Unique (DGU). Enforcement is active. Closures began in March 2025. The 17-30 June 2026 operation in Abobo, Anyama and Yopougon found 50-60% of venues without authorisation. The inspectorate targets 10,000 inspections in 2026, and there were 923 formal notices in 2025. No software or done-for-you competitor was found. The weak points are that it looks like a one-off onboarding wave, not a recurring duty, and renewal and validity were not found. The dossier is paper-based (10 copies), so it is a fixer service, not a software product. The tourism development tax rose to 2.5% in 2026, a minor recurring item. Buyers are informal and pay little. Market size is unquantified.

Duty is real in principle. A Water Ministry communique (reported Jun and Aug 2026) cites Law 2023-902 art. 12: prior authorisation or declaration for raw-water abstraction. It targets borehole operators, drinking-water operators, farms and agro-industry, mining, energy and tourism. Households are exempt. The communique gives no fee, penalty, frequency or inspection regime. I found no application decree and no fee schedule. The 1989 decree 961 tax needs a ministerial order and may be superseded. I found no portal, software or competitor. Market size was not found. The duty looks like a mostly one-off permit, aimed at larger users, with no confirmed enforcement date or recurring filing. That makes it a weak recurring-SaaS case, so I score it 3.

The duty looks real: at the 5 Mar 2026 Daloa launch the CCAK delegate said all buyers must be CCAK-approved, hold stores, and declare pisteurs tied to a single buyer. Boundiali also reported CCAK cards for pisteurs and buyers. A 2014 decree on FAOLEX requires a pisteur list for approval. I could not confirm that the decree is still in force, the penalties, or how often reports are due. I found no CCAK digital register and no competitor, though I searched only two queries. Wi-Agri is a private traceability platform for producers, not for buyer compliance. The number of approved buyers was not found. Approval is annual and paper-based. Buyers are informal, price-sensitive and hard to reach, so willingness to pay is low and the score stays at 3.
